artists.biography:
Tracy Chapman (born March 30, 1964) is an American singer-songwriter. Chapman is best known for her hit singles "Fast Car" (1988) and "Give Me One Reason" (1995).

Chapman was signed to Elektra Records by Bob Krasnow in 1987. The following year she released her debut album, Tracy Chapman, which became a commercial success, boosted by her appearance at the Nelson Mandela 70th Birthday Tribute concert, and was certified 6× Platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America. The album received six Grammy Award nominations, including one for Album of the Year, three of which she won: Best New Artist, Best Female Pop Vocal Performance for her single "Fast Car”, and Best Contemporary Folk Album. In 1989, Chapman released her second album, Crossroads, which earned her an additional Grammy Award nomination for Best Contemporary Folk Album. Her third album, Matters of the Heart, followed in 1992.

Chapman's fourth album, New Beginning, was released in 1995 and became another worldwide success. It was certified 5× platinum by the RIAA and yielded the hit single "Give Me One Reason", which earned Chapman the Grammy Award for Best Rock Song. Five years would pass before the release of her fifth album, Telling Stories (2000). Let It Rain and Where You Live followed in 2002 and 2005, respectively. Chapman's most recent studio album is Our Bright Future, was released in 2008. The remastered compilation album Greatest Hits, which was curated by Chapman herself, was released in 2015. In 2023, she became the first black woman to score a country number one with a solo composition when Luke Combs covered her song "Fast Car".

perplexity.description:
Tracy Chapman’s self-titled debut album, released in 1988 by Elektra Records, is a landmark in contemporary folk-rock. The album features a stripped-down, acoustic-driven sound that emphasizes Chapman’s clear vocals and socially conscious songwriting. Tracks like “Fast Car,” “Talkin’ Bout a Revolution,” and “Baby Can I Hold You” showcase her ability to blend personal storytelling with broader themes of social justice, economic hardship, and hope, all delivered with a sincerity rooted in the folk tradition but accessible to a mainstream rock audience.

As the first release in Chapman’s discography, the album established her as a major new voice in music and set the tone for her subsequent work. It was both a critical and commercial triumph, reaching number one on the US Billboard 200 and earning six-times platinum certification from the RIAA. The album’s success was amplified by Chapman’s performance at the Nelson Mandela 70th Birthday Tribute, which helped propel its singles onto international charts. Widely praised for its authenticity and emotional depth, Tracy Chapman remains one of the most successful and influential debut albums by a female artist in rock history.
